idiom: to keep an eye on something
meaning: to watch something carefully so that nothing bad happens to it
literal_translation: vigilar algo de cerca para que no ocurra nada malo
example: Can you keep an eye on my bag while I buy a drink?
origin: Refers to the eye as the body part used for watching and protecting

wrong_meanings.meaning: to close your eyes for a short sleep
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom means to watch carefully, the opposite of closing the eyes
The idiom is about paying attention, not about wearing glasses

wrong_meanings.meaning: to paint a picture of a face
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with painting or art

explanation: 'Keep an eye on something' means to watch it carefully, usually to make sure it is safe. It is common in everyday speech when asking someone to look after your things.
